keyVerseText: Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth: men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith. reprobate: or, of no judgment reprobate: or, of no judgment
rootMeaning: The name Ἰαννῆς (Iannēs) is of Egyptian origin, indicating a cultural and historical background distinct from typical Hebrew or Greek names found in the New Testament. While the root word is not provided, this proper noun identifies a specific individual known as Jannes, linking directly to an Egyptian context. This etymological detail enriches our understanding by situating the character within a particular ethnic and historical milieu rather than as a generic figure.
usageInScripture: This term appears only once in the New Testament, specifically in 2 Timothy 3:8, where it is translated as 'Jannes.' The singular occurrence and consistent translation emphasize the proper name of a known individual, rather than a descriptive term or title. This limited usage highlights the importance of this figure in typological contrast rather than as a broad theological concept.
theologicalSignificance: The mention of Ἰαννῆς (Jannes) in Scripture serves as a reminder of opposition to God's truth, represented historically by those who resisted Moses. Recognizing Jannes as an Egyptian adversary grounds the biblical narrative in real historical conflict, illustrating the enduring spiritual battle between truth and falsehood. For the Christian faith, this name symbolizes the persistent resistance to God's revealed will and the dangers of corrupt minds rejecting faith. It calls believers to discernment and steadfastness in truth, reflecting Christ’s victory over all opposition.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Timothy 3:8, the reference to Jannes and Jambres as those who withstood Moses vividly portrays opposition to divine authority and truth. The use of Ἰαννῆς here underscores the historical reality of this resistance, which Paul draws upon to warn against similar spiritual opposition in his own time. This word thus enriches the verse by linking contemporary false teachers with notorious figures of rebellion, emphasizing the seriousness of resisting the faith.
